prompts.text: What's an unexpected subject you'd enjoy discussing over a long walk with someone you fancy?
Tell me about a conversation that started with a tiny observation and turned into an entire evening.
Talk about funny childhood ambitions or share strange things you've learnt as an adult?
We're stuck in a lift for five harmless minutes. What question would you ask to make the time fun?
People often reveal their curiosity through the stories they choose to follow up.
An interesting conversation doesn't need to become a test of compatibility.
What's a question you would find charming because nobody usually thinks to ask?
Recall a time someone remembered an unfinished conversation and brought it up days later.
We both have one funny story we haven't told each other. Who should go first?
Finish a story in person or save the surprise ending for a voice note?
Which ordinary errand would make a surprisingly fun date with the right person?
Describe getting to know somebody better while completing a simple practical task.
Go grocery shopping for a shared recipe or hunt for a thoughtful gift for a mutual friend?
We're choosing ingredients for a meal neither of us has cooked. What's the first decision you want to make?
Small decisions reveal whether two people enjoy improvising together.
A date can feel special without a venue that requires booking.
What's an everyday skill you'd love someone you're seeing to teach you?
Tell me about someone turning a routine journey into something you remember fondly.
Our planned activity takes half the time we expected. How should we fill the unexpected free hour?
Make something together or try finding the best inexpensive snack nearby?
What's a harmless competition you'd challenge somebody you liked to?
Recall somebody playfully challenging you and accidentally revealing their competitive side.
A mini bowling contest or a race to solve a simple puzzle?
We make a friendly bet where the loser chooses a song for the winner. What's your strategy?
The way somebody handles losing can be as entertaining as the game itself.
Friendly competition is best when nobody feels obliged to pretend they're good at the activity.
Which little skill would give you an unfair advantage on a first activity date?
Describe a game where you were hopeless but laughed throughout it.
The scoreboard malfunctions and declares us both winners. How should we celebrate?
Teach each other a favourite game or pick a completely unfamiliar one?
What's a memorable way someone has shown they care about your interests?
Tell me about a person who asked you to explain a hobby they'd never tried.
Have someone join your favourite activity once or ask thoughtful questions about it afterwards?
We each get fifteen minutes to introduce an interest the other knows nothing about. What would you choose?
Taking an interest in someone's enthusiasm creates conversation even when preferences differ.
You don't have to share every hobby to appreciate why it matters to somebody.
What's a personal interest you'd rather explain face to face than through text?
Describe a time a new person surprised you by enjoying one of your favourite activities.
You invite me to see something you've been working on. What's one question you'd want me to ask?
Attend a beginner workshop together or take turns choosing short activities from our existing hobbies?
Which small sign tells you somebody enjoys your company rather than merely being polite?
Recall realising you were looking forward to hearing a particular person's opinion.
Someone laughing at your odd observations or remembering the question you asked last time?
We're saying goodbye and both suggest meeting again at exactly the same moment. How would you react?
Shared enthusiasm sometimes shows itself in the simplest choices about spending time.
Paying attention to what a person says matters more than trying to sound charming.
What's something you'd notice about a person after seeing them interact with close friends?
Tell me about a small respectful gesture that made someone more appealing to you.
A friend asks what you like about somebody beyond their looks. What would be your first answer?
A person who remembers your favourite jokes or one who spots your mood changing?
What's a funny assumption somebody might make about your ideal date?
Describe planning something you'd thought was your style and discovering you preferred a simpler outing.
A picnic with homemade snacks or a late afternoon walk that ends at a café?
A friend designs a date for you based on three clues. What three clues would you provide?
A person's dream outing often says as much about their energy levels as their interests.
Being able to say what you don't enjoy makes shared plans better.
What's an unusual place you'd love to visit with somebody who enjoys asking questions?
Recall somebody introducing you to a venue that wasn't your usual choice but suited you.
We each get to nominate one place for a relaxed Saturday. How do we decide the order?
Choose a familiar favourite and talk for hours or explore a new spot together?
What's a playful way to find out whether two people have matching senses of humour?
Tell me about a harmless joke that made you realise somebody understood your personality.
Trade amusing observations about the day or invent absurd scenarios for each other?
We have to write captions for the same ridiculous stock photograph. What style of caption would yours use?
Two people sometimes bond through laughing at details nobody else has noticed.
Someone who checks whether a joke landed is more attractive than someone determined to be funny.
What's a joke topic you'd want somebody to avoid until they knew you better?
Recall someone making a social situation easier by gently laughing at their own mistake.
Our harmless joke confuses somebody nearby. How would we explain without making anyone uncomfortable?
An ongoing inside joke or a new ridiculous question every time we meet?
What kind of shared memory would you want to create before calling something a relationship?
Describe an ordinary outing that helped you feel at ease around somebody new.
Take photos during a special moment or keep your phones away and enjoy it?
We decide to make a tiny souvenir from an outing instead of buying anything. What would we keep?
Meaningful early memories often involve details people didn't plan beforehand.
It's fine to value consistency over constant surprises in a developing connection.
What's a small promise someone might keep that would increase your trust in them?
Tell me about a moment when somebody's reliability impressed you more than a romantic gesture.
One of us has to cancel a plan unexpectedly. What response would help maintain goodwill?
Agree on a regular short catch-up or plan dates when our schedules align naturally?
Which topic would you enjoy learning about someone's family without becoming too personal?
Recall a funny family story somebody told you that revealed their sense of humour.
Share childhood nicknames or describe favourite family meals?
We're talking about how different households celebrate birthdays. What tradition would you tell me about?
Family stories often explain the little habits people carry into adulthood.
Respectful curiosity about someone's upbringing is better than making assumptions about their values.
What tradition from your upbringing would you enjoy showing somebody special someday?
Tell me about an elder whose humour influences the way you tell stories.
Your family has a saying that needs context. How would you explain it to someone you're getting to know?
Compare funny childhood rules or share stories about family celebrations?
What's something you'd want to understand about a person before making bigger plans together?
Describe a time somebody's honesty made a light conversation feel more comfortable.
Talk through a future plan as a hypothetical or focus on the next fun thing to do together?
We discover we organise our days in completely different ways. What's a playful way to compare routines?
Early connections become easier when people explain how they like to communicate.
A thoughtful question about boundaries is more appealing than treating every preference as a challenge.
What helps you feel comfortable telling somebody you need an evening to yourself?
Recall a person responding graciously when your plans changed at the last minute.
We both enjoy getting to know each other but have busy weeks ahead. How might we stay connected without pressure?
A short call when we're both free or a few thoughtful messages over the week?
